headline: The US Federal Trade Commission has demanded documents from OpenAI and Anthropic about safety incidents involving their AI models.
score_reason: Confirmed by an FTC spokesperson, two leading AI developers, a new formal step; headline matches the facts.
importance_line: A consumer-protection regulator is now compelling evidence on AI safety incidents, which affects the many people who use these chatbots and puts both companies under formal scrutiny, though a subpoena is not a finding of wrongdoing.
summary: Axios reports, as relayed by CBS News, that the Federal Trade Commission, the US consumer-protection regulator, has sent formal demands to AI developers OpenAI and Anthropic for documents on safety incidents, privacy policies and safeguards, and an FTC spokesperson confirmed the subpoenas. The step comes about two weeks after the agency said it was investigating the two firms, and Axios says subpoenas to outside organisations are due to follow.
notes: Original Reuters page blocked (401); read CBS News, which credits Axios.
